analysis.title: Anthropic Files Updated S1: Committed Spend Jumps To $900BN, Only Google Has More
key_insights: Anthropic's S-1/A shows Q3 2026 revenue of $16.96B, up 1,127% y/y and 47% q/q, versus 144% q/q growth in Q2. Growth was partially offset by about $600M of price reductions from new model versions and contractual discounts.

Q3 GAAP operating loss was $567M, after a $974M operating profit in Q2. The filing attributes it mainly to $5.0B of compute bought under short-term commitments and $2.0B of non-cash charges for the donation matching program.
Compute and infrastructure expense rose 77% q/q to $9.9B, or 58% of revenue versus 48% in Q2. Revenue per dollar of compute fell to $1.72 from $2.08, the first decline in the series.
The $5.0B of short-term compute costs significantly more than multi-year commitments. Anthropic procures compute 12 to 18 months ahead, so costs are generally fixed in the near term.
Non-cash donation-matching charge was $2.0B in Q3 versus $126M for the whole first half. Other operating and administrative expense rose to $3.6B (21% of revenue) from $1.0B in Q2.

Total operating expenses were 103% of revenue in Q3, up from 92% in Q2. Adjusted operating income for the first nine months is $4.1B (12% margin), implying about $2.5B in Q3 against the $567M GAAP loss.

Personnel expense fell to $1.7B from $1.9B and quarterly stock comp fell to $1.1B from $1.3B. Sales, marketing and partnerships fell to 14% of revenue from 22% in Q1, which the filing ties to lower channel-partner revenue share and changed distribution terms.
Unrecognized SBC on RSUs is $24.1B (plus $2.1B on other awards), and most of it is recognized when the S-1 goes effective.
Q3 net loss was $23.3B, of which $21.9B came from marking up convertible notes, derivatives and SAFEs. Nine-month net loss is $104.0B on $33.2B of revenue. Interest income was $1.2B.

Cash, equivalents and short-term investments were $131.8B at Sept 30 ($95.6B cash plus $36.3B short-term investments), flat from $131.7B in June. Accumulated deficit is $156.2B and stockholders' deficit is $149.9B. Redeemable preferred is unchanged at $157.5B.

Aggregate committed spend is approximately $895.4B, substantially all for compute and infrastructure: $320.0B in the contractual obligations table, $451.2B of leases not yet commenced, $100.2B of commitments signed after Sept 30, and about $24B of short-term commitments.
Deals without a fixed dollar commitment are estimated by Anthropic at $150B to $175B. Including them, the author puts the all-in total at roughly $1.05-1.07 trillion.

About $447.5B of commitments land before the end of 2030 and substantially all of the remainder falls between 2031 and 2045. Over 80% of Q3 revenue came from model versions released in the prior six months.

Google's hosting commitment was amended to at least about $121.3B (April 2026 to July 2033), from $114.5B in the original S-1. Other named deals: Broadcom $161.2B TPU lease rent, SpaceXAI up to $120.5B, Amazon at least $110B, Microsoft $44.9B, Nscale $44.6B, Lambda $41.3B.

About $69.8B of commitments are due in the 12 months after Sept 30. That compares with Q3 annualized revenue of $67.8B, more than half the cash balance, and about 11x nine-month operating cash flow of $6.6B. The author says commitments are 65x contracted backlog and 4x liquidity.

About $213.8B (24%) of commitments are subject to termination rights or contingent conditions, but only $4.3B of the next 12 months' bill has such an out. The contingencies depend on neoclouds such as Lambda and Nscale securing facilities and financing.

Broadcom's $42B note facility finances quarterly rent, carries 9% PIK interest convertible at 90% of 30-day VWAP, and steps to 13% PIK converting at 85% if revenue performance conditions are missed. Broadcom can demand 150% of principal on a change of control.
Google has an option to buy up to $10B of stock in a concurrent private placement at the IPO price, alongside a $20B note facility capped at 14.99% Google ownership.

Price range and share count are still blank. At the reported $1.5T valuation, Q3 annualized revenue of $67.8B implies about 22x revenue. The author leans toward the view that Anthropic is going public out of need rather than strength.

market_movers.rationale: Broadcom's $42B note facility to Anthropic carries a PIK rate that rises to 13% if revenue conditions are missed. The author calls it circular financing.

earnings_insights: Anthropic (private, S-1/A) reported Q3 2026 revenue of $16.96B, GAAP operating loss of $567M and net loss of $23.3B. All figures are reported GAAP, not estimates. Management had guided about $16.8B at its investor day.
Anthropic Q2 2026 GAAP operating profit was $974M (about 8% margin), reported in the earlier S-1.
risk_factors: Near-term commitments of $69.8B due in the 12 months after Sept 30 exceed Q3 annualized revenue.
Revenue growth is decelerating (47% q/q versus 144% q/q in Q2) while price cuts of about $600M were introduced in Q3.
Compute cost growth outpaced revenue growth, and short-term compute is bought at premium prices.

Neocloud counterparties' ability to secure financing determines whether commitments are cancellable, and a tighter AI credit market would also cut Anthropic's compute supply. The author cites CoreWeave CDS as narrowing.
The remaining unrecognized SBC of $24.1B on RSUs is recognized when the S-1 goes effective.
IPO proceeds are partly earmarked for tax withholding on RSU settlement.

tension_points.bull_case: Revenue is up 45x across the last seven quarters and grew 47% q/q in Q3. Roughly 24% of commitments carry termination rights or contingencies, and the author notes the mix should get cheaper if $5B of short-term compute rolls off as long-term capacity arrives.
tension_points.bear_case: Revenue growth is slowing with $600M of price cuts, compute grew faster than revenue, and $69.8B of commitments due in 12 months exceeds the $67.8B annualized revenue run rate. Only $4.3B of the next 12 months' bill has an exit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q4 compute cost staying elevated if the $5B of short-term compute does not roll off, or revenue failing to outrun the $69.8B of commitments due in the next 12 months.

theme_stances.key_argument: Commitments of $895B, with $70B due in 12 months, lean the author toward the view that the IPO is driven by need.
theme_stances.evidence: we lean a little more toward need

theme_stances.key_argument: Flexibility in Anthropic's commitments depends on neoclouds' ability to borrow, which hedges the wrong scenario.
theme_stances.evidence: That's a hedge that pays off exactly when you'd least want to use it.
